title: E-EVAL: A Comprehensive Chinese K-12 Education Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2024)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of a dedicated benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in Chinese K-12 education. The authors argue that existing general-purpose benchmarks and Chinese language benchmarks do not sufficiently capture the subject-specific, grade-specific, and culturally specific knowledge needed to assess LLM performance in primary, middle, and high school contexts.

To address this gap, the paper introduces E-EVAL, a comprehensive multiple-choice benchmark with 4,351 questions spanning 23 K-12 subjects, divided into arts and science domains. The items were collected from regional homework, practice questions, and mock exams sourced from schools and educational institutions, with manual processing to standardize formulas and verify answers. The study evaluates 15 open-source and commercial LLMs using zero-shot, few-shot-answer-only, and few-shot-chain-of-thought prompting.

The benchmark is not a teacher intervention or classroom deployment study; it is an evaluation paper focused on model capability rather than human participants. The results show that Chinese-dominant models generally outperform English-dominant models on Chinese K-12 questions, but all models perform better on arts than science, and many struggle with mathematics. The paper also finds that few-shot prompting usually helps modestly, while chain-of-thought prompting often lowers overall performance, though it can help on more structured science problems. The authors conclude that E-EVAL can support more rigorous assessment of LLMs for Chinese K-12 educational applications.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s conversational large language model system used for general-purpose question answering and generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as one of 15 LLMs on the E-EVAL Chinese K-12 benchmark under zero-shot, five-shot answer-only, and five-shot chain-of-thought prompting.

findings.finding_summary: On the full E-EVAL benchmark, ChatGPT achieved 54.6% average accuracy overall (Table 3/8), below multiple Chinese-dominant models and only modestly above random (25.0%). Under prompt variations, it improved from 54.5% zero-shot to 56.9% five-shot answer-only, but dropped to 52.3% with five-shot CoT, indicating limited and unstable gains from prompting.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: General large language model category / generic generative AI used for educational question answering and reasoning.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper benchmarks multiple general-purpose LLMs in Chinese K-12 education and analyzes their strengths and limitations as a class, including effects of few-shot prompting and chain-of-thought prompting.

findings.finding_summary: Across 15 evaluated models, performance was generally higher in arts than science and higher in middle school than primary school for top models. The paper also reports that few-shot prompting usually helped slightly, while chain-of-thought prompting had a negative impact on overall performance but helped complex science subjects such as mathematics.
findings.measure: Benchmark accuracy patterns across subject categories and prompt types

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark evaluation paper rather than a field or intervention study, so causal evidence about teacher coaching or lesson-plan feedback is absent. The methodology is systematic and transparent, but the evidence is limited to model benchmark accuracy.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports moderate-to-high benchmark performance differences, but these are not direct educational outcome effects and do not demonstrate classroom impact. The overall findings are informative for model capability assessment, yet they do not show clear positive or negative impact on teachers or students.
